title: The Other Nefertiti (2015)
content:
Comments

arketyp · Nov 14, 2026

>“The Other Nefertiti” talks about decolonizing our minds, democratizing culture, and activating artifacts. We strived to make this cultural object publicly accessible and to promote a contemporary and critical approach to how the so-called “Global North“ deals with heritage and the representation of “the Other.” We should tell stories of entanglement and deconstruct them. Nefertiti is an excellent case for telling stories that differ from the dominant narrative and seeing how they intertwine.

You can tell this is from 2015. Reads like parody nowadays. Don't get me wrong, I was into that writing too. And I'm into Nefertiti forever and ever.

vintagedave · Nov 14, 2026

Yes, and 'counter-intervention to imperial cleptomaniac continuities' is way over the top.

But I think we could do with more of that language still today: it was healthy protest. You can understand something better when you critique and reverse it, question inherent assumptions. 'Decolonizing our minds' is exactly that for a specific set of cultural backgrounds.

Whether you agree afterwards -- the conclusions you come to -- is different from the health of being able to do so.

vintagedave · Nov 14, 2026

> „Artists ‘steal’ Queen Nefertiti bust by secretly scanning and releasing 3D printing data online. The scanning was an act of protest against Western museums taking artifacts from abroad and claiming them as their own.“

> -- The Independent

I feel there's value in musueums having items from other places, and I would like to see a massive spread: the world is a big place and it helps to see how big. But what bothers me is that they say the museum appeared to have scanned data of the bust for years and didn't release it, ie claimed and retained exclusive ownership of that, and that is something it's harder to support.

A physical item has to be somewhere, in one location. Digital can be shared.

Secretly scanning and releasing the data about an item of immense importance is a wonderful act of protest, specifically because it highlights what the museum should have done, and did not.
